title: Annie Hall
events_chronological: Alvy Singer grows up in a house under the Coney Island roller coaster, depressed at nine because the universe is expanding.
At school Alvy kisses a girl in class, and his classmates stand up one by one to announce what they grew up to be.
Alvy does his army service entertaining troops and becomes a stand-up comedian in New York.
Alvy's first marriage, to Allison Portchnik, fails while he obsesses over the Kennedy assassination in bed.
Alvy's second marriage, to Robin, fails amid Manhattan literary parties and her refusal to be interrupted.
Alvy meets Annie Hall after a tennis game with Rob, and she drives him home terrifyingly and asks him up for wine.
Alvy and Annie's first date ends in bed, and afterwards she needs a cigarette.
Annie moves in with Alvy, who pushes her into adult-education classes and books about death.
Alvy sends Annie to an analyst and pays for it, and their two sessions are played side by side in split screen.
Alvy and Annie visit her family in Wisconsin, where Grammy Hall stares at him and he sees himself at the table as a Hasid.
Annie's brother Duane confides his urge to steer into oncoming headlights, and then drives them to the airport.
Alvy and Annie break up, and each of them tries seeing other people.
Annie calls Alvy at three in the morning about a spider in the bathroom, and they get back together.
Annie starts singing in clubs and is courted professionally by the record producer Tony Lacey.
Alvy and Annie fly to Los Angeles for a television award, and Alvy hates every minute of it.
On the flight home both of them admit, in voice-over, that the relationship is over.
Alvy flies back to Los Angeles to propose, is turned down in a health-food restaurant, and crashes a rental car.
Alvy writes a play in which the woman says yes, and admits to the audience that you can do that in art.
Alvy and Annie meet again in New York as friends, and he watches her walk away.
Alvy tells the joke about the man whose brother thinks he is a chicken, and says relationships are irrational but we keep going through them anyway.
syuzhet_notes: Alvy narrates straight to camera and moves by association rather than by clock, so the film announces the break-up at told-order bullet 5 before showing the meeting at bullet 6, and drops his two earlier marriages in at bullets 8-9, well after the affair they precede. Told-order bullets 2-4 are childhood and early-career flashbacks, and Alvy repeatedly walks into his own past scenes as an adult to argue with the people in them.
fabula_notes: The film gives no dates, so the ordering of the two marriages relative to each other and to Annie is inferred from Alvy's narration. The play at told-order bullet 19 is a fiction Alvy writes about events already shown, not a further event in the relationship.
